newsitem.title: UK: Major concedes defeat in British election.
newsitem.headline: Major concedes defeat in British election.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major conceded defeat in the British election on Friday.

Major, leader of the Conservative Party, said he had already telephoned Labour leader Tony Blair to offer his congratulations. "Tonight we have been comprehensively defeated," Major told supporters after winning his parliamentary seat at Huntingdon, north of London.
Major said he had wished Blair "every good fortune in the great responsibility he will have in the years that lie ahead".

"Elections always have winners and they always have losers. It is a very great occasion to win an election. We are a great and historic party, the Conservative Party, we have had great victories in our time, we have had defeats in our time.

"We accept them both with a certain dignity and a certain grace. Tonight we have been comprehensively defeated. We will listen to the voice of the electorate, we will consider what has been said to us," Major said.
Labour looks set for a huge majority in the 659-seat parliament after Thursday's election.
